name: Question 3
worked_solution:
The gradient of the function $f(x,y)$ is defined as

$$
∇f(x,y)=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\,i+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\,j.
$$

Since $∇f(x,y)=F(x,y),$ the function $f(x,y)$ must satisfy the following system:

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=y{e}^{xy},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x{e}^{xy}+2y
$$

First, we integrate $\frac{∂f}{∂x}$ with respect to $x.$ Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & =\int \frac{∂f}{∂x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int y{e}^{xy}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{xy}+g(y)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, differentiating the above expression with respect to $y,$ we obtain

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x{e}^{xy}+{g}^{′}(y).
$$

Taking $\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x{e}^{xy}+2y$ into account, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x{e}^{xy}+{g}^{′}(y) & =x{e}^{xy}+2y \\ {g}^{′}(y) & =2y \\ g(y) & ={y}^{2}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is a constant.

Finally, substituting $g(y)={y}^{2}+C$ into our expression for $f(x,y),$ we get

$$
f(x,y)={e}^{xy}+{y}^{2}+C.
$$

Question 3
?

Find f(x,y) such that ∇f(x,y)=F(x,y), where F(x,y)=yexy i+(xexy+2y) j.

a
f(x,y)=xexy+2+C
b
f(x,y)=yexy+x2+C
c
f(x,y)=exy+y2+C
d
f(x,y)=exy+xy+C
e
f(x,y)=xyexy+y+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The gradient of the function f(x,y) is defined as ∇f(x,y)=∂f∂xi+∂f∂yj.

Since ∇f(x,y)=F(x,y), the function f(x,y) must satisfy the following system: ∂f∂x=yexy,∂f∂y=xexy+2y

First, we integrate ∂f∂x with respect to x. Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of y: f(x,y)=∫∂f∂xdx=∫yexydx=exy+g(y)

Now, differentiating the above expression with respect to y, we obtain

∂f∂y=xexy+g′(y).

Taking ∂f∂y=xexy+2y into account, we obtain xexy+g′(y)=xexy+2yg′(y)=2yg(y)=y2+C, where C is a constant.

Finally, substituting g(y)=y2+C into our expression for f(x,y), we get f(x,y)=exy+y2+C.
